sourceInformation.source: B-17 Bomber (Mattel Electronics, Intellivision, 1982); original, unaffiliated adaptation
sourceInformation.genre: Arcade flight action with mission planning and station-based combat
sourceInformation.perspective: First-person pilot and four gun mounts, downward bombsight, overhead operational map, brief exterior views
sourceInformation.tech: HTML/CSS/ES2022 JavaScript; my-3D2dge 0.89.1 at 8ecc2f62353761187bdfe226f327b7ea5d2eb691; World3D; Three.js 0.182.0; Rapier SIMD compat 0.19.3; esbuild 0.25.12. Native fixed stepping at 120 Hz. Everything is embedded in one offline HTML.
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original procedural low-poly aircraft, cockpit, coast, harbor, cranes, military ship, refinery and airfield, using the engine's native pixel/cel style and olive, teal and amber palette
sourceInformation.animation: Native Humanoid math rigs and expressions; fixed-step aircraft bank and pitch, engine-dependent propellers, ailerons, gun traverse/recoil, bomb doors, gravity-driven bombs, fire/smoke, destruction and landing gear
sourceInformation.audio: Original code-synthesized score, four engine layers, guns, flak, bomb release/whistle, impacts, radio and warning effects; distinct pitched gibberish crew voices through native audio buses. First-run music volume is 10%. No audio files or browser speech synthesis. Original source recording timbres: unknown.
sourceInformation.online: Standalone solo and local horizontal split-screen co-op for 1-2 players; AI Hub Session Protocol 1/client 1.4.0 at 35a1047f2067b2af3de3943f0fe452f39105d869, shared-world 1-2 player co-op with authoritative host, periodic corrections, reliable actions/outcome, departure handling and playerless-server support. Standalone internet rooms are supplied by AI Hub.
sourceInformation.testing: Unrestricted headless state, native-input, browser, audio and full-playthrough tests; screenshots for composition. One quiet verification entrypoint. Tested all nine difficulty/loadout combinations, controller stubs, touch profiles/multitouch, split screen, audio analyser, file-origin/offline packaging, WebGPU, WebGL 2, and Hub normal/impaired network/departure/server scenarios. Physical controller, real touch hardware, TV and human listening were unavailable. No FPS targets or optimization milestone.
sourceInformation.research: Read preserved original instructions and developer history on history.blueskyrangers.com, preserved visual references on intvfunhouse.com, the native engine handoff/API/assets/flight/racing references, and the full current AI Hub contract and harness. Evidence and exact links are in docs/research.md.
sourceInformation.environment: Codex CLI (headless); Linux, Ubuntu on WSL2; Playwright 1.63.0 with the installed Chromium, WebKit and Firefox

testingFeedback: 18 distinct product issues were caught by scripted play, browser checks, screenshot inspection and contract/source inspection; fixes and evidence are recorded in docs/issues.md. Test-driver mistakes are listed separately and are not counted as product issues.
Two were critical: the first takeoff collided with the initial collision threshold, and native WebGL bloom hid procedural aircraft geometry. Both are fixed.

The full native-input sortie was most useful: it drove the public menus, takeoff, directional gunnery, flak, bomb release, map return and recovery. The Hub counterpart also verified a guest station claim and finite release, then a successful shared sortie.

The first isolated gun test was least useful before its authored mission waves were disabled; extra encounters made the test report unrelated kills. Correcting test isolation made it meaningful. Hardware feel and subjective listening remain unknown.
engineFeedback: The native 3D pen, fixed-step loop, Humanoid portraits, reusable Shell/settings and audio buses supplied a coherent foundation for a procedural game.

I initially trusted bloom and the split-overlay contract. WebGL screenshots exposed missing pen geometry; source inspection showed the camera foreground was explicitly skipped in split view, and scene entry resets split setup.

The main custom work was the coupled bomber simulation: flight/resources, six stations, ownership/handover, continuous weapon checks, shared bomb prediction, encounters, mission outcomes and the authoritative Hub adapter.
The hardest integration was keeping camera foregrounds, projected HUD, split view, input ownership and remote authority consistent while producing one portable offline file.

One World3D engine change: allow the rebuilt camera foreground to render in each split viewport and restore the renderer's previous auto-clear value. The full core engine is unchanged. Bloom is disabled in game configuration; packaging, flight, capability checks and networking are game-side additions.
I would add a tested portable single-HTML World3D example with embedded Rapier and working split-screen foregrounds to the handoff.
promptFeedback: The prompt identified the source's whole-aircraft responsibility and required complete outcomes, practical dev tools and evidence instead of a shallow shooting gallery.
The plan referred to a broader builder brief and planner-time model settings; TASK.md resolved the delivery names, metadata schema and max-effort model record.
The hardest part was sustaining navigation, defense, bombing and recovery as one readable game while supporting solo, couch co-op, touch and a playerless authoritative Hub host.
I would include the portable native 3D/Hub reference with the handoff and consolidate repeated delivery rules into one explicit acceptance checklist.

aiHub.name: B-17 Bomber Buddy
aiHub.tagline: Deliver the parcel. Bring the crew home.
aiHub.description: Plan a Channel crossing, defend four bearings, hold the bombsight steady and bring a vulnerable four-engine bomber home. Fly solo, share the stations on a couch, or crew the same aircraft through AI Hub.
aiHub.controls: WASD fly, mouse aim, E/Q power, 1 pilot, 2 guns, 3 sight, 4–7 bearings, Space/click fire/release, B doors, X salvo, M map, H hold, F extinguisher, hold J jettison, Esc pause; standard pad and contextual touch supported.
